diagnosis.root_cause: A splitter branch on EPON0/6 has failed, leaving at least five ONUs offline (including customer 22371) while other ONUs on the same PON port remain online.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds and reports online:0 for the subscriber, which is a definite current offline state.
The same EPON0/6 port has multiple other definite offline ONUs at indexes 15, 16, 20, and 46, while indexes 8, 13, 49, and 57 remain online.
Multiple offline ONUs with surviving peers place the failure boundary inside the PON port and identify a splitter failure rather than a single ONU fault or whole-port failure.

The subscriber's seven-day RX telemetry was stable around -22.4 to -23.1 dBm in the normal band, TX power was stable around +2.3 dBm, TX bias remained healthy near 11 mA, and distance stayed constant at 294 m; there is no evidence of fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, all eight tested PONs are reported healthy, and OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are normal, ruling out an OLT-wide failure.

The router heartbeat is healthy, the expected customer VLAN 1016 is present, RADIUS data is consistent, and the customer had only one session in the last 24 hours, so authentication, VLAN, router, and session-flapping faults do not explain the outage.

The OLT has 25 offline customers out of 298, which is above the approximate background baseline, but the direct per-ONU readings show the affected boundary is EPON0/6; the population total does not override that evidence.

remediation.action: Dispatch field technicians to inspect and replace or repair the EPON0/6 splitter and its affected branch/fibre connections. Verify all affected ONUs recover, confirm RX/TX readings return, and clear the mass-ONU-offline alarm. Do not replace the OLT or router; both are healthy. Treat the customer's historical optical readings as stable and the current zero/null readings as offline-state readings.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
